# Native window resource admission review

Copyright 2026 Hitesh Soliwal and contributors. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0.

## Recommendation

**Hold the skip-prefix native atom from performance admission.** Correctness and ABI qualification passed, but the frozen local CPU rule flags 18 of 196 cases. Ten flags execute the changed nonempty emission path; eight occur on unchanged control or empty paths. The source and all evidence remain available for review. The root owns the final admission decision.

The strongest repeated changed-path observation is the int last-only window of length 65,536 with row/state offsets 3/5. Its median paired candidate/baseline CPU ratio is 1.232535 (+23.25%); all six paired ratios exceed 1.0759. The int last-only length 4,097 at offsets 0/0 also exceeds 1.09 in every pair, with a median ratio of 1.215626. These observations prevent an unqualified CPU-improvement claim for the combined int/long atom.

## Method and evidence scope

The frozen plan and probe ran six counterbalanced fresh-JVM pairs, with three retained raw samples for each of 196 cases: two primitive widths, seven lengths, seven shapes and two independent offset pairs. All 12 measured JVMs exited successfully. Every output/checksum tape matched. All 7,056 timing samples and 2,352 retained-output observations remain in the round logs. The 13-command receipt includes strict probe compilation and all measured JVM invocations; every retained log hash was rechecked.

The runtime was the pinned Temurin JDK 21.0.8+9 on Linux x86-64, CPU affinity 0, fixed 128 MiB initial/maximum heap, Serial GC and -Xbatch. Both variants used the same pinned Java classes and their already qualified unsanitized C17 libraries. The timing slot began only after the full SDK worker explicitly became idle. The raw environment and command files record the exact setup.

The predeclared CPU flag requires a median paired ratio above 1.10 and at least four of six ratios above 1.05. Medians are computed within each JVM from its three samples before pairing. This is a local admission rule, not a confidence interval. No fastest-sample selection, sample deletion or repeat-to-pass was used.

## Every flagged case

Unchanged controls also fluctuate and some paired ranges are wide. That limits causal attribution for individual flags. The complete 196-case summary also contains improvements, particularly some large long windows; favorable cases do not erase the flagged int cases or justify a general speed claim.

## Allocation and process observations

Every raw paired timing sample has exactly equal measured allocated bytes: 3,528 of 3,528 pairs. Every per-JVM median allocation vector matches for all 196 cases. All 1,176 paired retained-output sets have an allocation difference of zero, with equal output counts and payload sizes. There are no allocation-increase flags and no measured Java allocation saving.

Both required ThreadMXBean counters and the optional process CPU/RSS observations were available in all recorded samples. Process CPU has coarse resolution and includes genuine zero deltas; unavailable values would have remained -1. Requested-GC heap deltas differ in 10 retained pairs, all in two empty int cases, and include runtime cleanup. Their range is -852,576 to 16,778,000 bytes in both variants. They are not exact output or native-scratch sizes.

Observed post-retention RSS ranges overlap: baseline 45,700–108,864 KiB and candidate 45,612–108,604 KiB. Per-process peak RSS ranges also overlap: baseline 105,648–109,212 KiB and candidate 105,440–108,820 KiB. These data do not establish a process-memory reduction. Whole-process elapsed/user/system CPU totals are retained in COMMANDS.jsonl and the recommendation JSON; they include warmup, requested GC, verification and printing and are not isolated kernel timings.

## Correctness and transfer evidence remain valid

Both complete native closures compile as C17 with strict warnings, link 11 libraries from 12 translation units, and preserve the generated JNI headers/export sets. A C++20 consumer checks generated-header types and C linkage. The model runs under UBSan and checks full actual exported compactor entrypoints through an instrumented JNI table. Actual checked-JNI Java runs separately establish runtime parity and expected unavailable/capability refusal behavior.

The instrumented model has 1,864 cases in each mode with matching semantic digest 2f94c174f2012771. State-count bytes (582,934) and state-emission bytes (503,560) are equal. Payload calls decrease from 2,324 to 1,954 and payload bytes from 3,021,360 to 2,304,828. This is finite model transfer evidence, not a measured JVM CPU result. The 1,024-row one-last-row representatives decrease payload transfer from 4,096 to 4 bytes for int and 8,192 to 8 for long; empty-count early return remains unchanged.

The actual additive Java/JNI contract checks 70,080 cases per backend, with identical digest c665315f798fc026, alongside the protected existing contracts. The initial full-SDK failure from omitted rank/signal native opt-in flags remains retained. Its correction changes only runner properties; the separate composed baseline and passes 4–6 each report 578/578 JUnit successes with no skipped/aborted tests. These later receipts supersede earlier stage-local NOT_RUN or retry-pending statements without altering them.

The available historical integrated libjava does not export the current core mask-window native entrypoints. The SDK shared-library results and resource measurements do not close the matching current-source integrated JDK image gate.

## Reproduction and publication custody

Read NATIVE_RESOURCE_PLAN.md and PRE_MEASUREMENT_CLARIFICATIONS.json before replay. The latter records a pre-execution wording correction (two required ThreadMXBean counters) and exact composed-baseline/free-block accounting, without changing the matrix, probe or thresholds. run_resources.py contains the bounded compile/measurement commands. Replays need fresh evidence directories and an exclusive timing slot; these existing artifacts are immutable.

SUMMARY.json and SUMMARY.csv retain all cases. ADMISSION_RECOMMENDATION.json records the recomputed flags, all allocation comparisons, process values and source/evidence seals. NATIVE_EVIDENCE_MANIFEST.json enumerates the native source templates, plans, runners, command logs and gate receipts for publication. Generated binaries are represented by the existing source/header/export/library seals rather than copied again.

Exclude the superseded design/native-tests/M3RequiredExcludedWindowContract.java and m3_required_excluded_window_regions.c from publication. Their additive replacement names are M3RequiredExcludedWindowRefinementContract.java and m3_required_excluded_window_refinement.c. The pinned original product fixtures remain protected and untouched.
